title: Step Processing Unit Contract

scope.purpose: Define the generic callable contract and execution responsibility of an actual pluggable processing unit coordinated by its owning Step.
scope.appliesTo: Every concrete Step Processing Unit selected by a concrete Step.

definition.name: StepProcessingUnit
definition.description: The actual callable processing unit that performs the processing responsibility assigned to its owning Step.
definition.architecturalNature: Processing implementation and callable execution boundary; not a wrapper whose sole responsibility is to delegate the processing to another unit.
definition.ownership: Each concrete Step Processing Unit realizes one Step processing responsibility within the composition of its owning Stage.

genericContract.name: StepProcessingUnit

typeParameters.name: TInput
typeParameters.meaning: The SPU-specific input type accepted by this processing unit and supplied by Step Composition.

typeParameters.name: TOutput
typeParameters.meaning: The SPU-specific processing artifact type that this processing unit may produce and carry in its invocation result.

input.name: input
input.meaning: The input value supplied for this Step Processing Unit invocation.

output.meaning: The structured aggregate result returned for this invocation.

genericContract.specialization: Each concrete Step Processing Unit binds TInput and TOutput to the types required by its own Step responsibility. The generic contract does not impose a common concrete input or output type across Steps.

responsibilities: Accept the input value conforming to its specialized TInput type.
Perform the actual specialized processing operation assigned to this SPU.
Return SPUExecutionResult[TOutput] for a normally completed invocation, preserving the results and evidence assigned to this SPU's invocation contract.
Define and register its own SPUErrorTypeDefinition instances through the SPUErrorTypeDefinitionRegistry Instance assigned to it by the Pipeline.
Create SPUError occurrences for errors arising within its own processing responsibility and make them available to the owning Step Composition.
Expose invocation-level results and occurrences needed by Step Composition without taking ownership of Step-level flow control.
Cooperate with applicable supporting units only where the concrete Step's composition contract assigns such interaction to the SPU.

executionContract.invocationUnit: One invocation of execute represents one execution attempt of the Step Processing Unit.
inputContract: The supplied input must conform to the concrete SPU's TInput type.
The generic contract does not prescribe the internal structure, ownership model, mutability, or lifetime of the SPU-specific TInput.
The generic contract does not prescribe whether the input is passed by value, reference, immutable view, or another language-specific mechanism.
processingContract: The Step Processing Unit itself performs its assigned specialized processing responsibility within the owning Step.
The implementation may use the optional supporting components defined for that Step.
The generic contract does not prescribe the order of validation, processing, error production, error handling, or observation.
The generic contract does not prescribe a linear, branching, iterative, or concurrent internal execution topology.
The Step Processing Unit creates SPUError occurrences for errors arising within its own processing responsibility, using definitions registered in its assigned SPUErrorTypeDefinitionRegistry.
The Step Processing Unit provides the SPUError occurrences it produces to the applicable ErrorResult construction or aggregation process according to the owning Step's Error Model.
The generic SPU contract does not prescribe a universal registration lifecycle or require error type definitions to be registered on every execute invocation.
returnContract: A normally completed invocation returns one SPUExecutionResult[TOutput].
The returned result uses the exact TOutput specialization declared by the concrete SPU.
SPUExecutionResult represents this SPU invocation only; it is not the aggregate result of the owning Step.
The owning Step Composition consumes the returned SPUExecutionResult and decides how it contributes to Step-level output and aggregate results.
A later failure within the SPU invocation must not cause previously produced result elements required by SPUExecutionResult to be discarded.

executionResultRelationship.producer: The concrete SPU assembles and returns its own invocation-level result.
executionResultRelationship.consumer: The owning Step Composition consumes the result and determines its contribution to StepExecutionResult.
executionResultRelationship.boundary: The SPU does not assemble StepExecutionResult and does not determine Step-level flow transitions.

supportingComponentRelationship.principle: Supporting components are internal collaborators selected and coordinated by the owning Step Composition; a concrete Step may associate a supporting unit with a particular SPU or with another Step-defined internal scope.

categories.name: Step PU Validator Units
categories.relationship: May perform validation and provide structured validator results for aggregation.

categories.name: Step Error Model
categories.relationship: Defines the Step-specific ErrorResult contract, its representation semantics, and aggregation rules for SPU error occurrences; it need not be a separate runtime object that physically performs aggregation.

categories.name: Step PU Error Handling Units
categories.relationship: May perform error-handling operations and provide a specialized structured THandlingOperationResult for each operation execution; the Step-specific error-handling composition represents these operation results in ErrorHandlerResult.

categories.name: Step PU Observation Units
categories.relationship: May observe execution and publish observability data independently of SPUExecutionResult.

constraints: No supporting component category is mandatory for every Step.
The Step Composition owns the association and orchestration of supporting-unit instances within the Step.
An SPU interacts with a supporting unit only where the concrete Step composition contract explicitly assigns that interaction to the SPU.
Each supporting component retains its own responsibility and structured result contract.
The SPU returns only its own SPUExecutionResult; it does not assemble StepExecutionResult.
The concrete SPU owns its SPUErrorTypeDefinition definitions and registers them through the Registry Instance assigned to it by the Pipeline; the Pipeline retains exclusive Registry ownership.
The concrete SPU creates SPUError occurrences for errors arising within its own processing responsibility and makes them available to Step Composition.
The Step Error Model defines ErrorResult semantics and aggregation rules; Step Composition performs the physical Step-level aggregation.
Each Error Handling Unit retains its own operation-specific result contract; Step-specific composition aggregates operation entries without collapsing distinct operation executions.
Target occurrence references use producerSPUIdentity plus occurrenceIdentity and do not embed or mutate ErrorResult.
Step Composition integrates ErrorHandlerResult as a separate optional field of StepExecutionResult.
The detailed callable input, per-operation result, identity, target cardinality, occurrence access, and lifecycle contract is defined by ../01.02_Step_Error_Handling/ErrorHandlingUnit_Contract.json.
Error Handling Units do not gain ownership of SPUError occurrences or permission to mutate ErrorResult through the occurrence-access surface.

stageRelationship.interaction: The Step Composition invokes the concrete SPU through its specialized StepProcessingUnit[TInput,TOutput] contract.
stageRelationship.boundary: The SPU performs its specialized processing and returns SPUExecutionResult; Step Composition owns the Step flow and Stage-facing Step result.
constraints: Stage Composition does not invoke SPUs directly; it invokes the owning Step through the Step contract.
The SPU does not expose its internal implementation to Stage Composition.
The SPU does not assemble StepExecutionResult or make Stage-level flow decisions.

explicitNonGoals: No common TInput or TOutput type is imposed across different Steps.
No universal execution context parameter is introduced.
No validator, error model, error handler, or observation component is made mandatory.
No fixed execution order is imposed on supporting components and processing.
No synchronous or asynchronous execution model is selected by this contract.
No exception type, exception propagation policy, catch boundary, or conversion of thrown exceptions into SPUExecutionResult is prescribed.
No concurrency, reentrancy, thread-safety, cancellation, or timeout guarantee is prescribed.
No constructor, dependency-injection mechanism, object lifecycle, or statefulness model is prescribed.
No language-specific interface syntax or implementation inheritance mechanism is mandated.
designConstraints: The SPU is the actual specialized processing unit, not a delegation-only wrapper.
The generic type parameters are specialized independently by each concrete SPU.
The logical execution operation accepts the SPU-specific input and returns SPUExecutionResult[TOutput].
SPUExecutionResult is scoped to one SPU invocation and is distinct from StepExecutionResult.
The owning Step Composition, not the SPU, owns Step-level orchestration and assembly of StepExecutionResult.
openDesignDetails: Confirm whether execute is the adopted public operation name or whether another callable name is preferred.
Decide whether execution requires an explicit ExecutionContext parameter in addition to TInput.
Decide whether the execution contract is synchronous, asynchronous, or supports both through distinct contracts.
Define the exception boundary and the relationship between thrown exceptions and the structured SPUExecutionResult contract.
Define cancellation and timeout behavior if required by the pipeline execution model.
Define whether concrete Step Processing Units may be stateful and what concurrency/reentrancy guarantees apply.
Define construction, dependency provision, and lifecycle ownership for concrete Step Processing Units.
Define whether a Step Processing Unit can be invoked more than once or concurrently by its owning Stage.

For every concrete Step using ErrorHandlingUnit publication, verify completion of 01.02_Step_Error_Handling/Single_Step_Publication_Specialization_Contract.json; the common SPU contract does not substitute for concrete Step definitions.

references.relationship: pre-execution reservation and result retention guarantee
publication acceptance, failure reconciliation, concurrency, and ordering
mandatory concrete publication and recovery specialization owned by each Single Step

errorTypeDefinition.responsibility: Define the SPU-specific error content and handling-action description types and register definitions through the assigned SPUErrorTypeDefinitionRegistry.

registry.ownership: The Pipeline exclusively owns and manages the Registry Instance and assigns one dedicated Instance to this SPU.
registry.SPUAuthority: The SPU uses its assigned Registry Instance to register and resolve its own error type definitions; this authority does not transfer Registry ownership.

occurrence.rule: The SPU creates an occurrence when an error arises within its own processing responsibility. Each occurrence references exactly one registered definition from its assigned Registry.

errorResultContribution.rule: The SPU provides its produced SPUError occurrences to the applicable ErrorResult construction or aggregation process.
errorResultContribution.contractOwner: The Step Error Model defines ErrorResult structure, representation semantics, and aggregation rules.
errorResultContribution.assemblyOwner: The owning Step Composition assembles the Step-level ErrorResult from occurrences made available by SPUs, according to the Step Error Model.
errorResultContribution.implementationFreedom: The Step Error Model need not be a separate runtime object that executes aggregation; Step Composition determines the implementation arrangement.

errorOwnershipAndProduction.exceptionBoundary: A thrown exception that prevents execute from returning SPUExecutionResult remains distinct from SPUError and is not automatically converted into an SPUError occurrence.

errorHandlingResultProduction.operationProducer: Applicable Step PU Error Handling Unit
errorHandlingResultProduction.operationResult: Each executed handling operation that returns a structured result provides its specialized THandlingOperationResult.
errorHandlingResultProduction.targetReferences: Each operation identifies its targeted SPUError occurrences through producerSPUIdentity plus occurrenceIdentity, as defined by the Step Error Model contract.
errorHandlingResultProduction.aggregateAssembly: The Step-specific Error Handling Composition, coordinated by Step Composition, assembles accepted operation entries into ErrorHandlerResult; Step Composition integrates that value into StepExecutionResult[TOutput].
errorHandlingResultProduction.separation: ErrorHandlerResult remains independent of ErrorResult and does not contain, mutate, or erase it.
errorHandlingResultProduction.lifecycleOwner: Step Composition owns the association, orchestration, and lifecycle/reuse decisions for Error Handling Unit instances. A unit may be associated with a particular SPU while remaining under Step Composition coordination.
errorHandlingResultProduction.invocationContract: Each Unit receives its specialized input and authorized occurrence access together with an invocation-bound OperationEntryPublisher. For every operation attempt, the Unit obtains a PublicationReservation before starting execution, assigns handlingOperationIdentity only after grant and before execution, and publishes the complete matching entry. The Publisher retains entries only at atomic acceptance; the Unit retains produced results before acceptance. The Step-specific composition reconciles ambiguous publication outcomes and aggregates accepted entries into ErrorHandlerResult.
identityRequirements: Each attempt has a distinct handlingOperationAttemptIdentity assigned before reserve.
Each actual execution has a handlingOperationIdentity assigned after reservation grant and before operation start.
Each entry preserves both identities and must match the reservation binding.
errorHandlingResultProduction.publicationOwnershipRule: The result remains under Unit responsibility until the Publisher atomic-acceptance point; calling publish or losing its acknowledgement does not by itself transfer or negate ownership.
errorHandlingResultProduction.stepContractCompletionRequirement: The owning Single Step contract must instantiate 01.02_Step_Error_Handling/Single_Step_Publication_Specialization_Contract.json, including concrete protocol result types, non-throwing complete-entry transfer, named Recovery Owner/procedure, identity generation, and status retention/expiry. The SPU is not fully specified for a Step using this path until these are complete.
errorHandlingResultProduction.recoveryCustodyRule: For pre-acceptance Publisher Contract Violation or indeterminate acceptance, the Step-defined Recovery Owner takes or retains custody of the complete result/entry under the Step recovery procedure. The SPU coordinates custody and preserves the result through exceptional termination.

stepCompositionRelationship.interaction: Selects and invokes the SPU, supplies its specialized input/dependencies, and consumes SPUExecutionResult.
responsibilities: Own the internal composition and flow decisions involving this SPU and other Step components.
Determine how this SPU's processingArtifact and other result elements contribute to Step-level output and aggregates.
Preserve producer SPU identity when incorporating SPUError occurrences into Step-level ErrorResult or occurrence references.
Keep exceptions that prevent SPUExecutionResult return distinct from returned structured results.
